answers.question: What's it for?
answers.answer: Just for me, to show friends

answers.question: What should it have?
answers.answer: My name, a few things I like, a photo spot

title: A page about me
summary: You'll build a simple personal page with your name, a spot for your photo, and a list of things you like, ready to show your friends.
outcome: A colorful one-page website about you that opens in any browser straight from your project folder.

simpler.title: Just the hello and your likes list
simpler.why: You'll build a real page that says hi and lists what you love, then give it a font, a coloured name, and a tidy list. Footer, card and photo can come later.

files.content:
🙂

Hi, I'm Sam!

Welcome to my little corner of the internet.

Things I like

  • 🍕 Pizza on Fridays
  • 🎮 Video games with friends
  • 🐶 My dog, Biscuit
  • 🎵 Loud music in the car

Made by me, 2024

steps.title: Build the page skeleton
steps.instruction: Make a new file called index.html. On the first line type <!DOCTYPE html>, which tells the browser this is a modern web page. Then add an <html> tag that wraps the whole page. Inside it, add an empty <head> (hidden info about the page) and an empty <body> (everything people see). Close each tag you open.
steps.why: Every web page in the world starts with this same frame.

checks.say: I can't find a file called index.html yet.
Something in your page looks broken. Check that every opening has a matching closing.
Your page frame isn't complete yet. Check you have the first line, the hidden part and the visible part.
checks.question: Does the file start with <!DOCTYPE html> and contain opening and closing html, head and body tags?

hints: A page has an outer wrapper, a hidden part for info, and a visible part for content.
Start with <!DOCTYPE html>, then <html>. Inside it put <head></head> and then <body></body>. End with </html>. Put each on its own line.

<!DOCTYPE …>
<html>
<head>
</…>
<…>
</body>
</…>

concept.title: Tags
concept.explain: Tags are words in angle brackets that tell the browser what each part is; most come in an opening and closing pair.

steps.title: Fill in the hidden info
steps.instruction: Inside <head>, add three lines. First <meta charset="utf-8">, which lets the page show every letter and emoji. Then a <title> with the text About Me: this is the name on the browser tab. Last, <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">, which connects a style file you'll make later.
steps.why: Your emoji will show properly and your tab gets a name.

checks.say: I can't see the line that lets your page show emoji yet.
checks.name: charset

checks.say: Your page doesn't have a tab name yet.
Your page isn't connected to style.css yet.
checks.name: href

hints: The hidden part needs three things: a letter setting, a tab name and a link to your style file.
Between <head> and </head>, add <meta charset="utf-8">, then <title>About Me</title>, then <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">.

<meta charset="…">
  <title>…</title>
  <link rel="…" href="…">

concept.title: The head
concept.explain: The head holds info about your page, like its tab name, that visitors don't see on the page itself.

steps.why: Every good page is signed at the bottom.

checks.say: I can't see the bottom strip with your signature yet.

hints: Add a bottom section to your page with a short sentence in it.

concept.title: Paragraphs and footers
concept.explain: A p tag holds a paragraph of text, and a footer holds the stuff at the very bottom of a page.

concept.title: Headings and boxes
concept.explain: h1 is the biggest heading on a page, and a div is a plain box you can name with a class and style later.

steps.title: Start your likes section
steps.instruction: Under </header>, add a <section>: a group of related content. Inside it, put an <h2> (a smaller heading) that says Things I like.
steps.why: Your page gets a clear second part.

checks.say: I can't see the part with the smaller heading for things you like.

hints: Make a new part of the page with its own smaller heading.
After </header>, type <section>, then an <h2> with Things I like, then </section>.

concept.title: Sections
concept.explain: A section groups content that belongs together, like a chapter in a book.

steps.title: List the things you like
steps.instruction: Under your h2, add a <ul>: a bulleted list. Inside it, add 4 <li> lines, one for each thing you like, each starting with an emoji: 🍕 Pizza on Fridays, 🎮 Video games with friends, 🐶 My dog, Biscuit, 🎵 Loud music in the car.
steps.why: Your favourite things appear as a neat list.
steps.expected:
• 🍕 Pizza on Fridays
  • 🎮 Video games with friends
  • 🐶 My dog, Biscuit
  • 🎵 Loud music in the car

checks.say: I can't see your list of 4 things you like yet.

hints: Make a bulleted list with four things you love.

Under the h2, type

concept.title: Lists
concept.explain: ul makes a bulleted list, and each li inside it is one bullet point.

quiz.question: Which tag makes one bullet point in a list?
quiz.explain: Each <li> is one item; <ul> wraps the whole list.

steps.title: Look at your page
steps.instruction: Open index.html in your browser (double-click the file). You should see your name, your list and your footer, still plain black and white.
steps.why: Seeing your page for real is the fun part!
hints: Find index.html in your folder.
Double-click it, or drag it onto a browser window.
If it opens in a text editor, right-click it and choose to open it with your browser.

steps.title: Pick a font and background
steps.instruction: Make a new file called style.css. Write a rule for body with font-family: Arial, sans-serif; (font-family picks the letter style) and background: #fdf3e7; (background is the colour behind everything, here a soft cream).
steps.why: Your whole page gets a friendly font and a warm colour.

checks.say: I can't find a file called style.css yet.
Your page background isn't cream yet.
Something in your style file looks broken. Check your curly brackets and semicolons.

hints: Tell the whole page which font and background colour to use.
Write body { }, and inside it font-family set to Arial, sans-serif and background set to #fdf3e7. End each line with a semicolon.

concept.title: Style rules
concept.explain: A style rule names what to change, then lists settings inside curly brackets, each ending with a semicolon.

steps.title: Colour your name
steps.instruction: Under the body rule, leave a blank line, then add a rule for h1 with color: #e8613c; (color sets the text colour, here a bright orange).
steps.why: Your name pops out in orange.

checks.say: Your big heading isn't orange yet.

hints: Give your big heading its own text colour.
Below the body rule, write h1 { } with color set to #e8613c inside.

concept.title: Text colour
concept.explain: color changes the colour of the words, and codes like #e8613c describe an exact colour.

steps.title: Space out the list
steps.instruction: Under the h1 rule, add a rule for ul with text-align: left; (text-align lines up text left, right or center). Then a rule for li with margin: 10px 0; (margin is the empty space outside a box: 10px above and below, 0 at the sides).
steps.why: Your list items get room to breathe.

checks.say: Your list items don't have space between them yet.
Your list isn't lined up on the left yet.

hints: Line the list up on the left, and add space around each item.
Write ul { } with text-align: left, then li { } with margin: 10px 0.

concept.title: Margin
concept.explain: Margin is the empty space around the outside of a box, pushing other things away.

steps.title: Turn the likes into a card
steps.instruction: Between the h1 rule and the ul rule, add a rule for section with background: white; and border-radius: 12px; (border-radius rounds the corners).
steps.why: Your list sits on a white card with soft corners.

checks.say: Your likes card doesn't have rounded corners yet.
Your likes card isn't white yet.

hints: Give the likes part a white background and round corners.
After the h1 rule, write section { } with background: white and border-radius: 12px.

concept.title: Rounded corners
concept.explain: border-radius makes the corners of a box round; bigger numbers make rounder corners.

steps.title: Size the card
steps.instruction: Inside the section rule, under border-radius, add padding: 20px; (padding is the space inside the box, between its edge and its words), margin: 20px auto; (auto centers the box), and max-width: 400px; (max-width stops the box getting wider than that).
steps.why: Your card becomes a neat, centered box.

checks.say: Your card isn't limited in width yet.
Your card needs some space inside its edges.

hints: Add room inside the card, center it and stop it getting too wide.
Under border-radius in the section rule, add padding: 20px, margin: 20px auto and max-width: 400px.

concept.title: Padding and width
concept.explain: Padding is space inside a box's edges, and max-width sets how wide a box can ever get.

steps.title: Center the whole page
steps.instruction: In the body rule, under background, add color: #333; (dark grey text), text-align: center;, margin: 0; and padding: 20px;. You've used all of these already!
steps.why: Everything on your page lines up in the middle.

checks.say: Your page isn't centered yet.
Your page text isn't dark grey yet.
Your page needs some space around its edges.

hints: Give the page grey text, center it, and swap the outside space for inside space.
Inside body, under background, add color: #333, text-align: center, margin: 0 and padding: 20px.

steps.title: Make the footer quiet
steps.instruction: At the very end of style.css, add a rule for footer with color: #999; (light grey) and font-size: 14px; (font-size sets how big letters are).
steps.why: Your signature is small and doesn't steal attention.

checks.say: Your footer text isn't small yet.
Your footer text isn't light grey yet.

hints: Make the bottom text lighter and smaller.
At the end of the file, write footer { } with color: #999 and font-size: 14px.

concept.title: Font size
concept.explain: font-size sets how big the letters are, usually in px (tiny dots on your screen).

quiz.question: Which one adds space INSIDE a box, between its edge and its words?
quiz.explain: Padding is inside the edge; margin is outside it.

steps.title: Style the photo box
steps.instruction: Between the body rule and the h1 rule, add a rule for .photo (the dot means 'the box with class photo'). Give it font-size: 80px;, background: #ffcf8a;, border: 5px solid white; (border is a line around the box), border-radius: 50%; (50% makes it round) and width: 140px; (width sets how wide the box is).
steps.why: Your emoji gets a big, round, framed spot.

checks.say: Your photo box isn't 140 wide yet.
Your emoji isn't big yet.

hints: Make the photo box big, orange, framed and round.
After the body rule, write .photo { } with font-size 80px, background #ffcf8a, border 5px solid white, border-radius 50% and width 140px.

concept.title: Borders and width
concept.explain: border draws a line around a box (thickness, style, colour), and width sets how wide the box is.

steps.title: Make it a perfect circle
steps.instruction: Inside the .photo rule, under width, add height: 140px; (how tall the box is), line-height: 140px; (the height of a line of text, which puts the emoji in the middle) and margin: 20px auto; to center it.
steps.why: Your photo becomes a perfect centered circle.

checks.say: Your photo box isn't tall enough to be a circle yet.
Your emoji isn't in the middle of its circle yet.
Your photo circle needs space above it.

hints: Make the box as tall as it is wide, and push the emoji to the middle.
Under width in .photo, add height: 140px, line-height: 140px and margin: 20px auto.

concept.title: Height and line height
concept.explain: height sets how tall a box is, and line-height sets how tall each line of text is.

steps.title: See your finished page
steps.instruction: Refresh index.html in your browser. You should see a round photo, your orange name and a white card of things you like. Show your friends!
steps.why: You built a whole web page yourself.
hints: Go back to the browser tab with your page.
Press the refresh button or F5.
If nothing changed, check both files are saved and in the same folder.
